## Measured state (2026-07-25)

Row-streaming coverage across the row-producing read surfaces:

| surface | `--stream` | `--format ndjson` |
|---|---|---|
| `list` | yes | yes |
| `search` | no | yes |
| `context` | no | yes (json/ndjson only) |
| `next` | no | no |
| `activity` | no | no |
| `graph` | no | no |
| `aggregate` | no | no |
| `deps` | no | no |
| `get` | no | no (json/toon) |

`events` is natively newline-delimited and is the shape everything else should converge on.

So there are three different answers to "give me rows I can pipe" — a dedicated `--stream` boolean, a `--format ndjson` enum value, and nothing at all — and the surfaces with no answer are precisely the ones that produce the largest row sets at scale: `graph` (4,352 edges today, millions later), `activity`, `deps`, `aggregate`.

## Why this is a scale primitive, not a flag tidy-up

At a million items the array-envelope shape is not merely verbose, it is unusable: both producer and consumer must materialize the full result before the first row is readable. `jq` on a one-million-element array buffers the array; `head -20` cannot terminate the producer early; an agent cannot start work on row 1 until row 1,000,000 is serialized. Line-delimited rows make the pipeline incremental in constant memory on both sides, and make `head`/`grep -m`/`xargs -n` terminate the producer through SIGPIPE.

This is the mechanical foundation of "pm composes with grep/jq/xargs" (pm-m9xv) at the scale pm-9rxu targets.

## Scope

1. One contract-declared streaming mode across every row-producing read; `--stream` and `--format ndjson` both remain valid spellings (alias-preserved, zero feature loss) but resolve to one implementation and one documented row schema per surface.
2. Rows are emitted incrementally as they are produced — a real generator/async-iterator path through the SDK, not a materialized array printed line by line. Gate this behaviourally: a bounded-memory test streams a large synthetic workspace with a heap ceiling, and an early-termination test asserts the producer stops on a closed pipe.
3. Envelope metadata (counts, cursors, truncation) that has no place in a row stream is emitted as a final trailer record with a declared discriminator key, so a stream is still self-describing and resumable via `--after`.
4. SIGPIPE/EPIPE handling is silent and exit-code-correct (the pm-psy1 shell contract governs the codes).

## Relationship to neighbours

- pm-srns owns the format-flag grammar and envelope spec — this item is the streaming shape that grammar must express, not a competing contract.
- pm-psy1 owns exit codes and stream discipline; the EPIPE behaviour is specified there.
- pm-plwm `--where` predicates keep selection O(result); streaming keeps delivery O(1) memory. Both are needed for million-item pipelines.
- pm-tuadp2 `--since` delta reads and pm-5gf0xf `--at` historical projection both produce row sets that inherit this shape.
Uniform row-streaming contract: every row-producing read emits incremental line-delimited rows in constant memory

Converge --stream and --format ndjson onto one contract-declared streaming mode available on every row-producing read surface, backed by a real incremental producer with a bounded-memory gate, a self-describing trailer record, and correct early-termination behaviour.

Every row-producing read (list, search, context, next, activity, graph, aggregate, deps) supports line-delimited row output through one contract-declared mode with both existing spellings preserved as aliases; rows are produced incrementally through an SDK iterator path, proven by a bounded-heap test over a large synthetic workspace and an early-termination test asserting the producer stops when the consumer closes the pipe; envelope metadata (count, cursor, truncation) is emitted as a final trailer record carrying a declared discriminator key so streams stay self-describing and resumable via --after; EPIPE is handled silently with the exit code declared by the pm-psy1 scripting contract; the row schema per surface is contract-declared and drift-gated; docs carry worked jq and xargs pipelines against a million-item workspace
